newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves new investments worth $344.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: India approves new investments worth $344.6 mln.

text.p: India's Industry Ministry on Thursday said it had approved 72 new foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals worth a total of 12.34 billion rupees ($344.6 million).

The latest approvals included a $49.9 million investment by Germany's Daimler-Benz AG to raise its stake in its joint venture with Tata Engineering and Locomotive Co Ltd (TELCO) to 76 percent from 51 percent, as well as new power-generation investments by Enron Corp of the United States.
A ministry statement said the approved investments covered power, software, consultancy, services, electronics and engineering services and were spread across the country.
The ministry said it had approved a total of 1,268 FDI proposals since July 1996 for investments totalling 248.36 billion rupees ($6.94 billion).

It said more than 5,972 FDI proposals involving investments totalling 1,016.83 billion rupees ($28.4 billion) had been approved since August 1991 when India launched a sweeping economic liberalisation programme.
